s.n: Three sets: $n(A\cup B\cup C)=\sum n(A)-\sum n(A\cap B)+n(A\cap B\cap C)$.

s.f: A\cap(B\cup C)=(A\cap B)\cup(A\cap C);\qquad A-B=A\cap B'

s.n: Equivalence = all three; it partitions the set into equivalence classes.

s.q: Only A, exactly one, exactly two (three sets)
s.f: \text{exactly one}=\sum n(A)-2\sum n(A\cap B)+3n(A\cap B\cap C)
s.n: Exactly two $=\sum n(A\cap B)-3n(A\cap B\cap C)$.

s.f: n(A\times B)=n(A)\,n(B);\qquad A\times(B\cup C)=(A\times B)\cup(A\times C)
\text{number of equivalence relations on an } n\text{-set}=\text{Bell number } B_n:\ 1,2,5,15,52
s.n: Smallest equivalence relation containing given pairs: add reflexive, symmetric and transitive closures.

s.q: Number of reflexive and symmetric relations / antisymmetric
Number of functions from A to B

s.f: f(-x)=f(x)\ (\text{even, symmetric about }y\text{-axis}),\qquad f(-x)=-f(x)\ (\text{odd, about origin})

s.n: $\sin^n x,\cos^n x$: period $\pi$ for $n$ even, $2\pi$ for $n$ odd; $|\sin x|+|\cos x|$: $\frac\pi2$. Period of a sum = LCM of periods (if it exists). $\{x\}$: period $1$.
Graph of $f^{-1}$ is the mirror of $f$ in $y=x$; $f$ and $f^{-1}$ meet on $y=x$ when $f$ is increasing.

s.f: \text{period of } |f| \text{ can be half that of } f\ (|\sin x|:\pi);\quad\text{LCM of } \tfrac ab,\tfrac cd=\frac{\operatorname{LCM}(a,c)}{\operatorname{HCF}(b,d)}
\sin x,\cos x:2\pi;\ \tan x:\pi;\ |\sin x|:\pi;\ \sin^4x+\cos^4x:\tfrac\pi2;\ \{x\}:1;\ \sin(\sin x):2\pi;\ \cos(\cos x):\pi
y=f(x)+k\ (\text{up}),\ f(x-h)\ (\text{right}),\ -f(x)\ (\text{flip in }x\text{-axis}),\ f(-x)\ (\text{flip in }y\text{-axis}),\ f(ax)\ (\text{squeeze})
s.n: $|f(x)|$: reflect the negative part up. $f(|x|)$: keep the right half, mirror it to the left.

s.f: f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\Rightarrow f(x)=kx;\quad f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)\Rightarrow k\ln x;\quad f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)\Rightarrow a^x

s.q: Range by AM–GM, quadratic in $x$, or monotonicity

s.f: \text{find the range of the inner function, then push it through the outer one}

s.q: Number of solutions of $f(x)=g(x)$ for periodic graphs
s.f: \text{count intersections over one period, multiply, then fix the ends}
f(x)=x\ \text{roots are where } y=f(x) \text{ meets } y=x

s: If this type comes, solve like this

s.q: If a relation on a small set is described and the number of its elements (pairs) is asked
s.r: "$xRy$ iff $2x+y\le2$ on $\{-2,\ldots,4\}$", "$(a,b)R(c,d)$ iff $2a+3b=3c+4d$", "$(x,y)R(z,w)$ iff $x\mid z$ and $y\le w$", "$R_1=\{(p,p^n)\}$".
s.s: Fix the first element $x$ and list all $y$ that work. || Add the counts over $x$. || For relations on $A\times A$ with independent conditions on the two coordinates, multiply the two counts. || Read off minimal/maximal properties (domain, range) from the list.
s.e: $x\mid z$ on $\{2,\ldots,6\}$: $3+2+1+1+1=8$ pairs; $y\le w$: $15$ pairs; total $8\times15=120$.

s.q: If the minimum number of pairs to add to make a relation reflexive/symmetric/transitive/equivalence is asked
s.r: "Minimum elements to add to $\{(a,b),(b,c),(b,d)\}$ to make an equivalence relation", "make $R=\{(x,y):\ln(x+y)\le2\}$ transitive".
s.f: \text{equivalence classes}: \text{an equivalence relation with classes } C_i \text{ has } \sum|C_i|^2 \text{ pairs}
s.s: For an equivalence relation, find which elements must end up in the same class (linked by any chain). || Count $\sum|C_i|^2$ and subtract the pairs already present. || For transitivity, list all pairs $(a,c)$ forced by $(a,b),(b,c)$ that are missing; repeat until nothing new appears.
s.e: $a\sim b\sim c$, $b\sim d$: one class of 4 elements → 16 pairs; add $16-3=13$.

s.q: If you must decide whether a relation is reflexive, symmetric, transitive or an equivalence
s.r: "$\gcd(a,b)=1$, $2a\ne b$", "$3ad-7bc$ is even", "$A\triangle B=\emptyset$ on the power set", "$3x+\alpha y$ multiple of 7 is an equivalence iff…", "$1+ab>0$".
s.s: Test reflexive with a general $a$ (and find a failing example). || Test symmetric by swapping. || For transitive, try small counterexamples (e.g. $\gcd(2,3)=\gcd(3,4)=1$ but $\gcd(2,4)=2$). || For parameter questions, impose reflexivity first; it usually fixes the parameter, then check the rest. || Count equivalence classes when asked (e.g. $\frac ab=\frac cd$ classes are fractions).
s.e: $3x+\alpha x\equiv0\pmod7$ for all $x$ ⇒ $\alpha\equiv4\pmod7$; then $3x+4y\equiv0\iff x\equiv y$, an equivalence.

s.q: If the number of relations with given properties is counted
s.r: "Symmetric relations on $\{1,2,3,4\}$ that are not reflexive", "reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, containing $(1,2)$, at most 6 elements".
s.s: Count the "free" pairs for the property and raise 2 to that power. || "Not reflexive" etc.: subtract from the total of the bigger class. || For small sets with several properties, list cases by hand (start with the forced pairs).

s.q: If it is about subsets of $A\times B$, inverse relations or relations defined by inequalities on integers
s.r: "Subsets of $A\times B$ with 3 to 6 elements", "domain of $R^{-1}$ for $x^2+3y^2\le8$", "sequence $(a_1,a_2),(a_2,a_3),\ldots$ in $R$".
s.f: n(A\times B)=n(A)n(B),\ \ \text{domain of } R^{-1}=\text{range of } R
s.s: Find the size of $A\times B$ and sum $\binom{N}{k}$ over the allowed $k$. || For integer-point relations, list the points satisfying the inequality. || For chains, follow the rule step by step to the longest possible sequence.

s.q: If it is a survey with two or three sets (at least / at most / exactly)
s.r: "220 students, at least 125 and at most 130 study Mathematics…", "25% read A, 20% read B, 8% both", "students numbered 1–140 opting courses by divisibility".
s.f: n(A\cup B\cup C)=\sum n(A)-\sum n(A\cap B)+n(A\cap B\cap C)
s.s: Draw a Venn diagram and give a variable to each region. || Translate each statement into an equation or inequality on the regions. || "Exactly one" $=\sum n(A)-2\sum n(A\cap B)+3n(A\cap B\cap C)$. || For bounds, push the variables to their extremes.

s.q: If it uses set identities or counts subsets (power sets, Venn statements)
s.r: "Subsets of $A$ are 56 more than those of $B$", "$\emptyset\ne A\cap B\subseteq C$; which is not true", "which Venn diagram fits the statement".
s.s: Write $2^m-2^n=56$ and factor: $2^n(2^{m-n}-1)=8\cdot7$. || Test statements with a small example set or a Venn diagram.

s.q: If a set is defined by number-theory conditions, or a word problem reduces to sets/equations
s.r: "$A=\{n:\gcd(n,45)=1\}$, $B$ even numbers up to 200; sum of $A\cap B$", "work done by two masons".
s.s: Translate into "not divisible by 3 or 5" type conditions. || Sum with AP formulas and inclusion–exclusion. || For work problems set up rates and solve.

s.q: If the domain of a composite function (logs, inverse trig, roots) is asked
s.s: List the condition for each piece, from the outermost function inwards (for $\log_a\log_b(\ldots)$: inner log $>0$, i.e. argument $>1$). || Solve each inequality. || Intersect all conditions. || For $f\circ g$: $x$ in the domain of $g$ and $g(x)$ in the domain of $f$.

s.q: If the range of a rational function is asked
s.r: "$f(x)=\frac{5-x}{x^2-3x+2}$ has range $(-\infty,\alpha]\cup[\beta,\infty)$", "$\frac{x^2+2x-15}{x^2-4x+9}$ is one-one/onto?", "$\frac{x^2}{1-x^2}$ surjective onto $A$".
s.s: Put $y=f(x)$ and cross-multiply into a quadratic in $x$. || For real $x$, discriminant $\ge0$: an inequality in $y$. || Remove $y$-values that need excluded $x$, and treat the case where the $x^2$ coefficient vanishes. || The resulting set is the range (for surjectivity, the codomain must equal it).

s.q: If the range of a trigonometric / inverse-trigonometric / log-of-trig expression is asked
s.r: "$\frac{\sin^4\theta+3\cos^2\theta}{\sin^4\theta+\cos^2\theta}$", "$2\cos^{-1}x+4\cot^{-1}x-3x^2-2x+10$", "$\log_{\sqrt5}(3+\cos(\ldots)+\ldots)$", "Sgn sums".
s.s: Reduce to one variable $t$ with a known interval. || Study the function of $t$ (monotonic? use derivative or simple bounds). || For log/exp outside, apply it to the inner range (direction depends on the base). || For sign functions, check each quadrant separately.
s.e: $\operatorname{Sgn}$ sum is $4,-2,0,-2$ in the four quadrants: range $\{4,0,-2\}$, sum $2$.

s.q: If the range of a sum of square roots, or of $[x]$-type compositions, is asked
s.r: "$\sqrt{3-x}+\sqrt{2+x}$", "domain of $\frac{[x]}{1+x^2}$ is $[2,6)$; range", "range of $f\circ g$ with piecewise $f,g$".
s.s: Square to get a constant plus $2\sqrt{\text{product}}$; the product is a downward parabola with a known max on the domain. || Min at an endpoint, max where the product is largest. || For piecewise compositions, find the range of the inner function on each piece, then apply the outer function.

s.q: If $f$ is composed with itself many times (Möbius map $\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}$)
s.s: Write the coefficient matrix. || Raise it to the power (diagonalise or spot a pattern). || Read the composite function and simplify by the gcd.

s.q: If onto functions or functions with value conditions are counted
s.r: "Onto $f:\{a,b,c,d,e\}\to\{1,2,3,4\}$ with $f(a)\ne1$", "$f(1)+f(2)=f(3)$", "$f(x)\le(x-3)^2+1$", "$f(mn)=f(m)f(n)$", "onto $f:S\times S\to S$ with symmetry".
s.s: Count all onto maps with inclusion–exclusion. || Use symmetry for a single-value restriction: each value is equally likely for $f(a)$. || For sum conditions, count pairs $(f(1),f(2))$ that make $f(3)$ valid; multiply by free choices. || For bounds, multiply the number of allowed values for each $x$.

s.q: If one-one functions with extra conditions are counted
s.r: "One-one $f:A\to B$ with $f(1)+f(3)=14$", "$2f(a)-f(b)+3f(c)+f(d)=0$", "$f(1)\ge3$, $f(3)\le4$, $f(2)+f(3)=5$", "one-one $f:S\to P(S)$ with $f(n)\subset f(m)$".
s.f: \text{fix the constrained values first, then } {}^{m}P_{k} \text{ for the rest}
s.s: List the allowed values (or pairs) for the constrained elements — distinct values only. || For each case, the remaining elements are mapped one-one into the remaining values: ${}^{m}P_{k}$. || Add over cases.

s.q: If increasing functions, or bijections with an order condition, are counted
s.r: "Strictly increasing $f:\{1..6\}\to\{1..9\}$ with $f(i)\ne i$", "bijections with $f(3)\ge f(9)\ge f(15)\ge\cdots$".
s.f: \text{strictly increasing } A\to B:\ \binom{|B|}{|A|};\ \ \text{ordered block of } k:\ \binom nk(n-k)!
s.s: An increasing function is just a choice of the image set. || With an order condition on $k$ elements, choose their $k$ values ($\binom nk$, order forced), then arrange the rest freely. || Subtract bad cases (like $f(i)=i$) by inclusion–exclusion if needed.

s.q: If functions $g$ with $g\circ f=f$ (or $f\circ g$ given) are counted, or $f$ is evaluated on a special set
s.r: "$f(k)=k+1$ for odd $k$, $k$ for even; number of $g$ with $g\circ f=f$", "$f\circ g(n)$ given; find $g$", "$f$ on the prime factors of 2310".
s.f: g\circ f=f\iff g(y)=y\ \text{for every } y \text{ in the range of } f
s.s: Find the range of $f$. || $g$ is forced on the range; free elsewhere. || Count $|\text{codomain}|^{\#\text{free points}}$.

s.q: If one-one / onto / bijective must be decided
s.r: "$f(n)=$ highest prime factor of $n$", "$\frac{2^x-2^{-x}}{2^x+2^{-x}}$ from $\mathbb R$ to $(-\infty,1)$", "$g\circ f$ with piecewise $f,g$", "$g(3n+1)=3n+2,\ldots$".
s.s: Check monotonicity with the derivative or a pair of equal values. || Find the range and compare with the codomain. || For piecewise functions, check each piece and whether the pieces overlap in values.
s.e: $\tanh$-type $\frac{2^x-2^{-x}}{2^x+2^{-x}}$ is increasing with range $(-1,1)\ne(-\infty,1)$: one-one, not onto.

s.q: If a functional equation of Cauchy type ($f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ or $f(x)f(y)$) is given
s.s: Recognise the type and write $f(n)$ in closed form. || For a modified type, put $y=0$, $x=0$, or $y=1$ to get a recurrence, then solve it. || Use the closed form in the sum and solve.

s.q: If a functional equation links $f(x)$ with $f$ of a transformed argument ($\frac1{1-x}$, $\frac1x$) or a cos-type rule
s.s: Substitute the cycle values to get a system of equations. || Add/subtract to isolate $f(x)$. || For the cos-type rule $f=\cos(kx)$; for cumulative sums, subtract the equation at $x-1$ to get a recurrence.

s.q: If $f(g(x))$ is given and another composite value, or $g$ as the inverse of an odd polynomial, is asked
s.r: "$4g(f(x))=3x^2-32x+72$ with $g(x)=3x^2+2x-3$", "$g(f(x))=x$ for $f(x)=\alpha x^5+\beta x^3+\gamma x$".
s.f: g(f(x))=x\Rightarrow g=f^{-1};\ \ \text{odd increasing } f\Rightarrow f^{-1}\text{ odd}
s.s: Put $u=f(x)$ and solve $g(u)=$ the given expression (a quadratic in $u$); choose the branch using a known value like $f(0)$. || For inverse questions, use symmetry (odd functions) and the fact that $f$ is strictly increasing.

s.q: If $\sum f\left(\frac kn\right)$ is asked where $f(x)+f(c-x)$ is constant
s.s: Compute $f(x)+f(c-x)$ for the natural $c$ (here $c=4$). || Pair the terms $k$ and $60-k$. || Count the pairs and the middle term.

s.q: If the inverse of a function is asked
s.s: Put $y=f(x)$ and solve for $x$. || Swap letters. || For $f=f^{-1}$ with $f$ increasing, solve $f(x)=x$ instead.

Write $x=n+f$ with $n$ integer and $0\le f<1$. || Substitute; the equation splits into an integer part and a fractional part (or gives $f$ in terms of $n$). || Impose $0\le f<1$ to get the allowed $n$. || For sums of $[\ ]$, find where the value jumps and count the terms in each block.

s.q: If the number of real roots must be found by graphs or monotonicity
s.s: Simplify where possible (logs combine into $|\sin2x|=\ldots$). || For polynomials, find critical points and check the sign of $f$ at them. || For piecewise right sides, sketch both graphs and count intersections.

s.q: If a power series or a determinant defines $f$ and a value is asked; or even/odd parts
s.r: "$f(x)=\sum kx^k$; $2f(2)+f'(2)$", "$y=\frac12x^2+\frac23x^3+\cdots$; $e^{1+y}$", "determinant $f(x)$ with $a-2b+c=1$", "$a^x=f_1+f_2$ (even + odd)", range of $y=x\ln\frac25$-type relation.
s.s: Recognise the series as a derivative or integral of a GP. || Simplify the determinant with row operations before differentiating. || Even part $\frac{a^x+a^{-x}}2$: then $f_1(x+y)+f_1(x-y)=2f_1(x)f_1(y)$.
